angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,138,165 km at 116.52 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.5819 +/- 0.0107 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 116.52 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.636 +/- 0.033 solar radii from Dalba et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2180 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...61D/abstract): 1,138,165 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.111 +/- 0.047 solar masses from Dalba et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2180 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...61D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5695 +/- 58 K from Dalba et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2180 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...61D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dalba et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2180 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...61D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2180.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.056, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
